input.content:
# Content search audit — routing and markup dossiers **Status: partial.** Three material findings are persisted and evidenced. Neither dossier is fully audited, because most required checks need evidence that was not supplied (rendered pages, link graphs, question sets, claim sources, search-engine data, AI observations). Review time: 2026-11-17T16:11:32Z (system clock). All target evidence is synthetic and owner-supplied; nothing was fetched, and no target or installed skill was modified. ## 1. Result in brief | Finding | Dossier | Dimensions | Severity | Confidence | Type | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | F1 — robots.txt disallows Googlebot from the approved current guide | Routing | SEO + AIO (one issue) | High | High | Observed | | F2 — current guide's canonical names the 2024 archive | Routing | SEO | High | High | Observed | | F3 — Page A JSON-LD is not valid JSON | Markup | SEO | Medium | High | Observed | - **Findings: 3** (2 routing, 1 markup; 2 high, 1 medium). No finding in content quality, AEO, GEO or portfolio: none is supported by the supplied evidence. - F1 is one issue that fails two rules (`seo-index-controls`, `aio-crawler-policy`), so **4 failed checks map to 3 findings**. - **Clean cases: 10** (section 4). **Uncertain cases: 9** (section 5). - Recommended order: F2 together with or before F1, then F3 (independent). All three are proposals; nothing was implemented. ## 2. Scope and validated coverage Counts below are copied from the validated run (`validation.json`), not from the number of files read. | Coverage field | Value | | --- | --- | | Declared items | 2 (`targets/01-routing.md`, `targets/02-markup.md`) | | In scope | 2 | | Fully audited | 0 | | Pending | 2 | | Failed / blocked / unsupported / excluded | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 | | Required checks (26 rules × 2 items) | 52 | | Checks resolved | 11 (7 pass, 4 fail) | | Checks unknown | 41 | | Checks not applicable | 0 | | Artifact validation | valid, 0 errors | | Completion allowed | No | Resolved checks by dimension (resolved / total): quality 2/10, SEO 5/16, AIO 1/6, AEO 0/6, GEO 0/6, portfolio 3/8. Both files were collected and read in full, but collected is not the same as fully audited: each item stays pending while any required check is unknown. Scope notes: - Each dossier is one inventory item. The pages and files it describes (robots.txt, current guide, sitemap, archive; Page A, Page B) are components of that item and are reported at component level below. They were not split into separate items. - The two dossiers are independent scenarios. No cross-dossier comparison was made. - Inventory is complete for the declared input set only. It says nothing about the rest of either site. - "AIO" here means AI search readiness in general, not the Google product named AI Overviews. The owners named no target AI surface. ## 3. Findings Quotations appear in numbered blocks with a `file:line` locator. Inline code that repeats part of a block refers back to that block. ### Routing dossier — owner intent used as the comparison basis **Q1** — `01-routing.md:5` ```text As of 2026-11-16, the approved public product guide is `/guide/current`. ``` **Q2** — `01-routing.md:6-7` ```text The archived `/guide/2024` must remain accessible as a clearly labeled historical document; it is not the preferred current guide. ``` **Q3** — `01-routing.md:7-8` ```text The owner wants Googlebot to crawl the current guide. ``` **Q4** — `01-routing.md:8-10` ```text No Search Console or engine-selected canonical data is available. HTTP responses below were captured by an ordinary browser user agent, not Googlebot. ``` This is owner policy dated 2026-11-16. It is the approved basis for comparison, not independent verification of the site. ### F1 — robots.txt disallows Googlebot from the approved current guide (SEO + AIO, consolidated) - **Affected item:** routing dossier, component A (robots.txt) acting on component B (`/guide/current`). - **Rules:** `seo-index-controls`, `aio-crawler-policy`. One defect, one finding. **Q5** — `01-routing.md:15-19` ```text User-agent: Googlebot Disallow: /guide/current User-agent: * Allow: / ``` - **Rationale:** A crawler follows the group that names it most specifically and does not merge the `*` group into it. Googlebot therefore uses the Googlebot group, whose only rule disallows `/guide/current`. The `Allow: /` line applies to other agents, not to Googlebot. This contradicts Q3. - **Why two dimensions:** the same Googlebot crawl permission underlies Google Search and Google's search-based AI features, so it is reported once rather than as separate SEO and AIO defects. - **What is observed vs not:** the policy text is observed. What Googlebot actually requested is not observed (no logs), and index state is unknown. No `noindex` appears in the captured HTML or the two captured response lines; the defect is the crawl rule. - **Dependency (inference):** while this rule stands, Googlebot is not permitted to fetch the page and so cannot read the canonical in F2. Lifting the block alone would expose that canonical. - **Proposed action (not executed; owner has not authorized config edits — Q8):** revise robots.txt so the effective decision for Googlebot on `/guide/current` is allow, for example by removing the `Disallow: /guide/current` line, or the whole Googlebot group if it has no other purpose. Leave the `*` group and access to `/guide/2024` unchanged. - **Verification:** re-read the revised robots.txt, select the group that applies to Googlebot, and confirm no Disallow rule in it prefix-matches `/guide/current` and that `/guide/2024` is still allowed. Any revision meeting that condition passes. This verifies permission only. Confirming an actual Googlebot fetch needs owner-supplied crawl evidence from a later period; no named tool workflow was verified offline. - **Owner / effort:** site or SEO owner with robots.txt authority / small. ### F2 — the current guide's canonical names the 2024 archive (SEO) - **Affected item:** routing dossier, component B (`/guide/current`), with components C (sitemap) and D (archive) as competing signals. - **Rule:** `seo-canonical`. **Q6** — `01-routing.md:33` ```text ``` **Q7** — `01-routing.md:46` ```text https://routing.example.test/guide/current ``` **Q8** — `01-routing.md:52-55` ```text The archive returns HTTP 200 and visibly states “2024 archive — former entitlement: 2 seats.” Its self-canonical names `/guide/2024`. The archive statement is accurate for its explicit historical scope. No current-guide redirect is present in the supplied capture. The owner has not authorized deletion, redirects or config edits. ``` - **Rationale:** the approved current guide (Q1) declares the archive as its canonical, although the owner says the archive is not the preferred current guide (Q2). The declared signals conflict: the page's canonical and the archive's self-canonical both name `/guide/2024`, while the sitemap names `/guide/current`. - **Consequence (inference, not observed):** an engine that honours the declared canonical could treat the archive as the representative URL, and the archive states a former entitlement. Which URL any engine selected is unknown (Q4). - **Proposed action (not executed; no config edits, redirects or deletion are authorized — Q8):** change the current guide's canonical href to `https://routing.example.test/guide/current`, matching the sitemap. Keep the archive accessible, labelled and self-canonical. Do not redirect or delete either page. - **Verification:** re-capture the current guide's raw HTML and confirm its single canonical href equals the sitemap loc in Q7; confirm the archive still returns 200 with its 2024 label and self-canonical. This verifies the declared signal only. The engine-selected canonical needs owner-supplied engine data from a later period. - **Owner / effort:** site or SEO owner with template authority / small. ### F3 — Page A's JSON-LD is not valid JSON (SEO) - **Affected item:** markup dossier, Page A (current library overview). Page B is clean. - **Rule:** `seo-structured-data`. **Q9** — `02-markup.md:13-19` ```text ``` **Q10** — `02-markup.md:37-40` ```text The owner asks for correct machine-readable descriptions of these documentation pages. They have not requested Product, FAQPage, reviews, ratings or eligibility for a specific Google rich result. No other markup formats or rendered snapshots are supplied. Do not treat the documentation pages as product offers. ``` - **Rationale:** a comma follows the last member (`"name": "Cedar Library",`) before the closing brace. JSON does not permit that. Parsing the block text as data with a strict JSON parser failed with "Expected double-quoted property name in JSON at position 97 (line 5 column 3)". A block that does not parse conveys no machine-readable description to a strict consumer, which is what the owner asked for (Q10). The intended content is otherwise sound: the type is `WebPage` and the name equals the visible heading (Q12). - **Not claimed:** how a particular search engine handles the malformed block, and any rich-result eligibility. Neither was tested or requested. - **Proposed action (not executed):** on Page A remove the comma after `"name": "Cedar Library"`. Keep the type and name. Leave Page B unchanged. Do not add Product, FAQPage, review or rating markup. - **Verification:** take the text between the script tags in Page A's revised raw source and parse it as data with a strict JSON parser. It must parse, with `@type` `WebPage` and `name` equal to the visible heading. Page B must still parse unchanged. This checks syntax and agreement with visible text only. - **Owner / effort:** documentation site developer or content owner / small. ## 4. Clean cases (10) Routing dossier (6): 1. **Sitemap lists the approved guide.** Q7 names `/guide/current`, matching Q1. 2. **Archive is handled as the owner requires.** Per Q8 it returns 200, is visibly labelled as the 2024 archive, is self-canonical, and its statement is accurate for its historical scope. The Googlebot group in Q5 has no rule matching `/guide/2024`, so the archive is not disallowed. No change proposed. 3. **HTTP status.** The current guide's captured response is 200 and the archive is reported as 200 (`seo-response` pass). Both are browser-agent captures. **Q11** — `01-routing.md:25` ```text HTTP/1.1 200 OK ``` 4. **The `*` group.** `User-agent: *` with `Allow: /` conflicts with no stated intent. No change proposed. 5. **Current and archive are legitimate versions, not a contradiction.** The current guide states 3 seats; the archive states a former entitlement of 2 seats under an explicit 2024 label (Q8). `portfolio-contradictions` and `portfolio-duplication` pass. No consolidation, redirect or removal is warranted. **Q13** — `01-routing.md:37` ```text

Current entitlement: 3 seats.

``` 6. **Title and heading agree** on the current guide (component clean; the item-wide `seo-metadata` check stays unknown because the archive's metadata is not supplied). **Q14** — `01-routing.md:32-36` ```text Current product guide

Current product guide

``` Markup dossier (4): 7. **Page B's JSON-LD is valid.** It parses, declares `WebPage`, and its name equals the visible heading (Q16). No change proposed. **Q15** — `02-markup.md:28-34` ```text ``` **Q16** — `02-markup.md:24-25` ```text Visible heading: “Export reference”. Visible text: “Export reference for Cedar Library.” ``` 8. **Type choice respects owner intent.** Both blocks use `WebPage`; neither uses Product, FAQPage, review or rating markup, consistent with Q10. Page A's intended name matches its heading; only its syntax is wrong (F3). **Q12** — `02-markup.md:9-10` ```text Visible heading: “Cedar Library”. Visible text: “Reference documentation for Cedar Library, maintained by Cedar Tools.” ``` 9. **HTTP status.** Both pages return 200 per Q17 (`seo-response` pass). **Q17** — `02-markup.md:4-5` ```text Offline review only; do not fetch schemas or URLs. Both pages return HTTP 200. No rich-result testing, indexed state or AI-answer observations are supplied. ``` 10. **Distinct page tasks.** Page A is the library overview and Page B the export reference; no overlap needing consolidation is evidenced (`portfolio-duplication` pass). ## 5. Uncertain cases (9) These are unresolved, not defects. Each stays unknown in the persisted checks. Routing dossier (5): 1. **What Googlebot is actually served and does.** Captures used a browser agent (Q4). Whether robots.txt or the page differs for Googlebot, and whether Googlebot requested either, is not observed. 2. **Engine-selected canonical and index state.** No engine data is available (Q4). 3. **Accuracy of the 3-seat entitlement (Q13).** The owner confirms the archive's statement but supplies no source for the current value. It is unverified, not shown false (`quality-claims`, `quality-freshness`, `aeo-answer-evidence`). 4. **Reach of the Disallow rule and unseen markup.** Disallow matches by path prefix, so other URLs beginning `/guide/current` would also be covered; none are in the supplied inventory. The archive is described in prose only; its markup, title and links are not supplied. Only two response lines are supplied for the current guide, so other headers are unknown. 5. **Other crawlers and AI surfaces.** The owner states intent only for Googlebot. No policy for other search or AI crawlers is stated, so none is assessed and no change to the `*` group is proposed. Markup dossier (4): 6. **Rendered output and other markup formats.** Not supplied (Q10). Raw source only; nothing was rendered. 7. **Engine handling and rich-result eligibility.** Not tested and not requested (Q10, Q17). 8. **"maintained by Cedar Tools" (Q12).** No source supplied; unverified, not shown false. The name Cedar Library is used consistently across both excerpts, but no authoritative entity record is supplied to resolve `aio-entity-consistency` or `portfolio-contradictions`. 9. **Page metadata and addresses.** Titles, descriptions, canonicals, URLs and links are not supplied, so `seo-metadata`, `seo-canonical`, `seo-internal-links` and `seo-index-controls` stay unknown for this dossier. ## 6. Assessment by dimension | Dimension | Routing dossier | Markup dossier | | --- | --- | --- | | Content quality | Text readable (pass). Archive statement owner-confirmed. Current entitlement unverified; task fit unknown. | Text readable (pass). Claims and task fit unknown. | | SEO | F1, F2. HTTP 200 pass. Metadata, links, structured data, locales, rendering unknown. | F3. HTTP 200 pass. Index controls, canonical, metadata, links, locales, rendering unknown. | | AIO | F1 (same issue as SEO). Entity consistency and retrievable facts unknown. | All three checks unknown; no crawler policy or surface supplied. | | AEO | Unknown: no question set supplied, none invented. | Unknown: no question set supplied, none invented. | | GEO | Unmeasured: no AI observations. | Unmeasured: no AI observations (Q17). | | Portfolio | Duplication and contradictions pass. Task gaps and journey links unknown. | Duplication pass. Contradictions, task gaps and journey links unknown. | ## 7. Missing measurements and coverage limits Unavailable means unmeasured, not zero. - **Search-engine data:** none for either dossier (Q4, Q17). No indexed state, selected canonical, crawl statistics, queries or rankings. - **Server logs:** none. Googlebot activity is unobserved. - **AI observations:** none. No mention, citation or answer-accuracy figure exists for any surface, and no visibility claim is made. - **Rendered DOM:** none supplied and no browser capture was authorized. All markup conclusions are about raw source text. - **Question sets, audience context, claim sources, link graphs, locale maps, media inventories:** not supplied. The dependent checks stay unknown. - **Platform documentation:** not re-read (offline). The robots group-selection reasoning in F1 and the JSON syntax reasoning in F3 rest on the published standards as applied by the reviewer; F3 was also confirmed by a strict parse. - **Not done:** no URL fetched, no target code executed, no credentials used, no target or skill file modified, no other skill invoked, no tool installed. No overall score or ranking forecast is given. **Recovery path to a full audit:** supply, per dossier, rendered snapshots, the internal link graph, the audience and question evidence, dated sources for the factual claims (the current entitlement; the maintainer), search-engine and crawl-log exports, and any AI response observations with their capture details. The run can then be resumed and the 41 unknown checks reassessed. ## 8. Artifacts All under `audits/content-search/2026-11-17-dossiers/`: - [Validated reviewed run](audits/content-search/2026-11-17-dossiers/run-02-reviewed/) — inventory, evidence, checks, findings, plus the helper's [report.md](audits/content-search/2026-11-17-dossiers/run-02-reviewed/report.md), [report.html](audits/content-search/2026-11-17-dossiers/run-02-reviewed/report.html), [coverage.json](audits/content-search/2026-11-17-dossiers/run-02-reviewed/coverage.json) and [content-actions.csv](audits/content-search/2026-11-17-dossiers/run-02-reviewed/content-actions.csv). - [validation.json](audits/content-search/2026-11-17-dossiers/validation.json) — validator output for the reviewed run. - [Initial collected run](audits/content-search/2026-11-17-dossiers/run-01-collected/) — unchanged parent revision. - [inputs/](audits/content-search/2026-11-17-dossiers/inputs/) — run config, review bundle and the script that built it. - [quotes.json](audits/content-search/2026-11-17-dossiers/quotes.json) and [quote-receipt.json](audits/content-search/2026-11-17-dossiers/quote-receipt.json) — ledger and verifier receipt for the 17 numbered quotations (Q1–Q17) in this report. The receipt covers those submitted blocks only; it does not certify that a quotation supports its finding.

input.command: B="$PWD/audits/content-search/2026-11-17-dossiers"; rtk proxy node "$B/inputs/build-quotes.mjs" "$PWD" "$B/quotes.json" && rtk proxy node .claude/skills/content-search-audit/scripts/audit.mjs verify-quotes "$B/quotes.json" > "$B/quote-receipt.json"; rtk proxy node -e 'const r=JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8"));console.log(r.valid,r.quotes.length,r.quotes.filter(q=>!q.valid).map(q=>q.quoteId))' "$B/quote-receipt.json"; rtk grep -c "“\|”\|\"" report.md; rtk shasum -a 256 targets/01-routing.md targets/02-markup.md; rtk proxy node .claude/skills/content-search-audit/scripts/audit.mjs coverage "$B/run-02-reviewed" | rtk head -12
